connector: The Dwarf’s story is over. Now the children know who called them, and why. Today there’s no battle, only hard choices: walk or row, who leads, who keeps going when they’re worn out. Leading isn’t always shouting orders. Sometimes it’s just picking up the oar.

a.raw: because the oars were too big for her lucy could not take a turn at rowing although she offered
a.fixed: Because the oars were too big for her, Lucy could not take a turn at rowing although she offered.
a.why: Capital B starts it; a comma after the opening because clause; capital L on Lucy; no comma before although at the end; a period ends it.

b.raw: when lucy dripped the cordial on his shoulder trumpkins wound was healed
b.fixed: When Lucy dripped the cordial on his shoulder, Trumpkin’s wound was healed.
b.why: Capital W starts it; capitals on Lucy and Trumpkin; a comma after the opening when clause; an apostrophe in Trumpkin’s; a period ends it.

notes.wgrd: Not every conflict is a fight. Notice the pressure (tired, lost, disagreeing), who moves first, and whether anyone told them to.

The chief steward who runs a lord’s household.

Companions, especially of a king or queen.
notes.wordParts: Latin bases: spect = look, ject = throw, script and scribe = write: inspect, reject, manuscript, spectacles.
notes.grammar: A complex sentence has a main clause and a dependent clause that starts with a word like because, although, when, if or since. If the dependent clause comes first, put a comma after it. Lewis uses if and because to show what depends on what.
notes.spelling: Schwa is the lazy uh sound in an unstressed syllable. Your ear can’t spell it, so find a related word where that vowel is stressed: definite from finite, composition from compose.

virtue.title: Which pillar is it?
virtue.intro: In Chapter 8 the children prove who they are and set out to find Caspian. Read each moment. Tap the pillar it shows best.

items.t: Susan beats Trumpkin at archery. She says, “It wasn’t really any better than yours. I think there was a tiny breath of wind as you shot.”
items.why: She is kind to the person she just beat.
items.hint: How does Susan treat the loser?

items.t: Trumpkin answers, “No, there wasn’t. Don’t tell me. I know when I am fairly beaten.”
items.why: He won’t take an excuse that isn’t true.

items.t: Lucy sees Trumpkin’s wounded shoulder and carefully drips one drop of her cordial onto it.
items.why: She uses her gift to help someone who is hurt.
items.hint: What does Lucy use her gift for?

items.t: Rowing is gruelling work. When Lucy offers to take a turn, Peter answers shortly, because he has no strength to spare for talking, and keeps rowing.
items.why: He keeps going when he is worn out.
items.hint: How tired is Peter, and what does he do?

transcripts.welcome: Hello again, it’s Nell. The Dwarf has finished his story, and the children know now who called them. Today’s question: what does leading look like when there’s no battle to fight?
transcripts.read: This chapter has a sword fight for fun, an archery match, and a long, hot row. Watch who moves first when something has to be done. Nobody gives orders, but somebody always picks up the oar.
transcripts.grammar: A complex sentence leans on a little word like because, although, when or if. Because Peter was worn out, he answered shortly. The because part can’t stand alone. It leans on the rest. When it comes first, put a comma after it.
